I view AI not as a threat to human creativity but as a profound evolution of our tools for expression. Imagine if we had “un-invented” photography because it changed painting, or word processors because they transformed writing. In each case, the art didn’t disappear—it adapted, expanded, and reached new heights. AI offers a similar opportunity to deepen human creativity, not diminish it.

Far from making human effort pointless, collaboration with AI can help us explore uncharted creative territories, express ideas we didn’t know we could, and even reimagine what it means to be an artist. The heart of art—its emotion, meaning, and connection—remains uniquely human. With AI as a creative partner, we’re not losing our place in the creative process—we’re gaining a new perspective on what it means to create. While this shift may be difficult and even painful at times, it holds the potential to transform art and creativity into something richer, more expansive, and more inclusive than ever before. column36: I never intentionally use chat bots, however every damned service in the world is trying to hop on the hyped-up and poorly designed bandwagon. I'm intelligent enough to not NEED help unless my particular circumstances place me into an edge case that an FAQ, a chat bot, or an automated process CAN'T FIX. column38: All of the listed options are things I do just fine on my own, better than a chat bot could in my estimation. column40: As mentioned above, I only ever use chat bots when I'm forced to interact with them as a part of a customer service process. My opinion of their capabilities and usefulness are very low as a result of those experiences.
column41: I understand that every business on the face of the Earth has to deal with hordes of brain-dead customers, daily, who can't be arsed to do the most basic research or even be trusted to find the company's website and click on the great big link in the middle of the page that will answer their question, and yes, I understand that handing these walking vegetables off to a chat bot to screen or herd is an efficient use of a business' resources, BUT FOR THE LOVE OF GOD stop assuming that a chat bot is capable of doing much beyond reciting a FAQ or doing basic call screening for your actual customer service representatives. Large language models do not, and will not for the foreseeable future, have the ability to replace line-level customer service employees or perform even the most basic customer-faced interactions without royally fucking up even MORE than a drugged-up high-school dropout call-center hire.

column41: I don't know where to start here. AI is still in its early stages and people are both optimistic and fearful about its potential. People are both frustrated with AI's inaccuracies and the fact that it doesn't seem to know everything from the onset of its existence. While also being fearful of its all-knowing, all-seeing Skynet people replacing, famine causing future. It all really doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me because those fears are often overblown. Especially when those in the media, that have no background in anything technological start fearmongering. It harkens back to when the Today show hosts were musing to each other "have you heard of this internet?" Ai is a tool, currently it is very helpful to me and will become more helpful in the future. It makes learning easier and more streamlined. It gives me information and places to look further to understanding the topics that I am interested in. I understand Ai's potential and have to parse the bullshit coming from people that are all shouting into the void about its negative consequences. I have to figure out which of those voices aren't just imbeciles barking nonsense and which of those are genuine inevitabilities. Nonetheless, AI is here to stay, and I will be utilizing it to the best I can. You either have to adapt to and understand the technology that controls our lives otherwise you are at a disadvantage.
